body:
Hi Mira,

Perfectly reasonable - we completely understand the need for PI approval on unpublished dissertation data. Your timeline (response by Jan 22-24) works well for us.

To answer your questions:

1. **Other datasets**: 11 labs contributing Th17/Treg trajectory data from mouse (barrier tissues: gut, skin, lung) and human (IBD biopsies, psoriasis lesions). Mix of 10x Chromium and SMART-seq2. Total ~180,000 cells across all datasets.

2. **Authorship**: We're using ICMJE criteria. Data contributors with significant datasets (>10,000 cells, novel biological contexts) receive middle authorship. Technical integration and writing team are first/last authors. You'd likely be 4th or 5th author based on current contributions.

3. **Embargo**: Confirmed. ImmPort deposition will have embargo flag until you provide your Chapter 3 acceptance notification. We can also delay our own preprint if that helps your timeline.

One additional note: if Dr. Harrison has concerns about premature release impacting your first-authorship priority, we're happy to have a three-way call to discuss safeguards. Several other grad students in the consortium faced similar considerations.

Looking forward to hearing from you next week.

Best,
Rachel

subject: Re: Chapter 3 committee feedback - trajectory methods
body:
Hi Mira,

I finally had a chance to review the trajectory analysis draft you sent earlier this month. Overall the approach is solid, but I have concerns about how you're handling the batch effects between your two experimental cohorts.

The ComBat-seq correction you're using can sometimes over-correct and create artificial smoothness in pseudotime trajectories. Have you tried running Slingshot on the uncorrected data as a sensitivity check? If the major trajectory structure holds up, that would strengthen your conclusions significantly.

Also - Jennifer [Thompson] mentioned you're working on the same dataset for your Immunity revision. Make sure the statistical approaches are consistent across both documents. Reviewers (and committee members!) will notice if you use different correction methods.

I'm traveling Feb 3-10 but available for a call the week of Feb 10 if you want to discuss before your committee report is due. Let me know.

Best,
Maria

--
Dr. Maria Rodriguez
Assistant Professor, Immunology
Stanford University School of Medicine

subject: Re: Metadata-first workflow implementation questions
body:
Hi Mira,

Glad the paper was helpful for your workflow optimization project! Happy to answer your implementation questions.

> How do you handle the offset timing between job phases?

We use a 5-minute offset between phases to avoid race conditions. Phase 1 (parallel RSS fetch) runs at :00, Phase 2 (serial import) runs at :05, Phase 3 (backlink generation) runs at :15. The key is making sure each phase has enough buffer time - we've found 5 minutes works well for up to 20 papers, but you might need 10 minutes if you're doing PDF downloads in Phase 2.

> What's your batch size limit for Zotero imports?

We cap at 20 papers per session to stay well under the 100 req/hour rate limit. Each paper uses 3 requests (metadata + PDF + collection assignment), so 20 papers = 60 requests with 40-request buffer. We've never hit rate limit issues with this sizing.

> How do you handle failure modes?

We have a health check job that runs 30 minutes after the main workflow to verify integrity. It checks for:
1. Orphaned Zotero records (no Obsidian backlinks)
2. Broken Obsidian links (citation_key doesn't exist in Zotero)
3. Failed PDF downloads (metadata imported but PDF missing)

If any issues are found, it sends an alert email with specific record IDs to fix. We don't try to auto-fix because that can make things worse - better to review manually.

One tip: Test your failure modes explicitly during pilot testing. We deliberately broke things (killed Zotero API mid-import, deleted PDF files, corrupted RSS feeds) to make sure the system failed gracefully. You want to know how it breaks before it breaks in production.

Let me know if you have other questions!

Best,
Jisoo

Salk Institute / UCSD

subject: Decision update: Declined Immunity review invitation (IMMU-2026-00234)
body:
Hi Dr. Harrison,

I wanted to update you on a decision I made today. I received an invitation from Immunity to review a manuscript on Th17 trajectory analysis (IMMU-2026-00234) - the topic was extremely relevant to Chapter 3, and under normal circumstances would have been a great opportunity for career capital and literature exposure.

However, given our recent conversations about Chapter 3 being six weeks overdue and the committee's growing concern about my timeline, I declined the invitation. The review deadline was April 25th, which would have fallen right in the critical period when I need to be finalizing the Chapter 3 discussion and preparing the progress report.

I cited dissertation timeline constraints in my response to the editor and indicated I'd be available for future reviews post-defense.

I wanted you to know that I'm taking your feedback about prioritization seriously and making decisions that align with getting Chapter 3 back on track.

Best,
Mira
